53	
54	### W1 — Harness capability program
55	
56	Goal 1 — the harness that makes any LLM the best agentic coder. An archive-first search over harness variants: every run is stamped in its own session log, parents are sampled from an archive that keeps losers, the mutator never touches the evaluator, and only a staged paired experiment plus an attributable human promote a variant into source.
57	
58	| Stage | Actor | Type | Status | Emits | Plugins | On failure |
59	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
60	| 1. Model matrix intake | Scorekeeper | D | partial | `CapabilityMatrix` | existing: llm, agent-default-model, agent-presets, bundle patch layers; new: model and preset overrides on `EnvironmentRunRequest` | A route without a registered adapter is excluded and named in the matrix. |
61	| 2. Suite selection | Scorekeeper | D | partial | `SuitePlan` | existing: environments; new: `EnvironmentStats` (pass@k per policy version), seed and topP on `LlmCallConfig` | An empty split fails loud; a held-out environment never enters a training or mutation cell. |
62	| 3. Fleet run | Fleet Orchestrator + environment runner | D | partial | `EnvironmentRunStamp`, `VerificationRun`, `EnvironmentRunReport` | existing: environment-runner, fleet, budget-policy, workflow, subagent providers, sandbox / E2B; new: idempotent cells by header hash × environment × repetition | A cell that cannot boot is a row with an error code, never a missing row. |
63	| 4. Facts projection | Scorekeeper | STORE | proposed | `ScoreboardBatch` | existing: trajectories, session-projection; new: scorekeeper `SessionFacts` projection plus leaderboard store | A metric without a source event is not a field. |
64	| 5. Diagnosis | Trajectory Analyst (cross-model) | DS | proposed | `SessionDiagnosis` | existing: session-query, subagent `outputSchema`; new: trajectory-analyst preset | Evidence seqs that do not exist reject the diagnosis; an environment-defect label opens a dispute, it retires nothing. |
65	| 6. Parent selection | Archive sampler | D | proposed | `ParentSample` | existing: storage; new: `dsh-archive` (`HarnessVariant` records over `ctx.storage`) | An empty archive is seeded with master as generation zero. |
66	| 7. Patch proposal | Harness Engineer (quarantined) | S | proposed | `HarnessPatchProposal` | existing: components, bundle patch layers; new: `harness-lab` preset, content-addressed component versions | A proposal touching an evaluator-owned path is a hard reject, never a directive. |
67	| 8. Novelty and static gates | run-gates + archive | GATE | proposed | `NoveltyVerdict`, `GateReport` | existing: scripts/run-gates; new: novelty gate | Findings return to stage 7 as the directive. |
68	| 9. Staged evaluation | Experiment service | D | proposed | `ExperimentResult`, `HarnessVariant` | existing: environment-runner; new: experiment plugin (ladder, paired design, confidence intervals, cost), `dsh-archive` | Inconclusive results park the variant; they never promote by default. |
69	| 10. Auditor and council | Review council (cross-model, no stake) | S | proposed | `ReviewVerdict` | existing: subagent `outputSchema`; new: oversight-seam judge council | Blocking findings return to stage 7. |
70	| 11. Promotion | Attributed human signer (component owner) | HUMAN | partial | `PromotionDecision`, `SignoffRecord` | existing: .agents/notes process, approval seam; new: `signoff/recorded` event, `decidedBy` on `approval/decided` | A rejection stays in the archive with its reason. |
71	| 12. Leaderboards | Scorekeeper | STORE | proposed | `ScoreboardBatch` | new: scorekeeper | — feeds W4 facts and W3 calibration. |
72	
73	`@deepseek-ai/dsh-fleet`'s `LeaderboardRow` (stage 3, implemented) already carries `provider`, `model`, `environmentId`, `environmentKind`, `heldOut`, `isolation?` (absent when every cell of the row failed before a run), `runs`, `errors`, `certified`, `certificateRate`, `attemptsMean`, `inputTokens`, and `outputTokens`, one row per model route and environment, so W1's model matrix already folds today from certificates alone; it is a fold of one fleet run; cross-run comparison, paired designs, and confidence intervals stay stage 9's job over the session logs.
74	
75	Parent selection (stage 6) draws a variant from the archive in proportion to quality × novelty × 1/(1+children) within islands per environment kind, and seeds an empty archive with master as generation zero, so the sampled parent — never `master` directly — is what the quarantined Harness Engineer mutates.
76	
77	The Harness Engineer's `harness-lab` preset carries no scored `ctx.goals` or `ctx.completionStandards` and no `tool-cordis` façade over environments, standards, or trajectories, and every proposal is content-hashed and frozen before the novelty gate or the staged evaluation runs, so nothing semantic can retarget its own evaluation after seeing a result.
78	
79	Staged evaluation (stage 9) runs a three-stage ladder — eight training-eligible environments at one repetition, then the diagnosis-and-lineage-derived cells at k paired repetitions with bootstrap confidence intervals, then the held-out suite once per Pareto-front variant and never shown to any semantic stage — and every result is archived alive or dominated, never discarded; a model-visible text change still requires a human diff review at promotion, and a snapshot re-record is never automatic.
80	
81	### W2 — Certificate-first software factory
82

Compile the signed spec into hidden standards before anything else, run every goal as its own session under a program ledger, let the runner validate against a tree hash, admit humans where authority must be attributable, and release only what a certificate on the merged head proves.

213	Efficiency (18 fields, all D, no council additions): `turns`, `steps`, `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cache_read_tokens`, `cache_write_tokens`, `reasoning_tokens`, `tokens_per_step_p50`, `tokens_per_step_p95`, `context_peak_tokens`, `cost_estimate_eur`, `kv_prefix_reuse_ratio`, `compaction_events`, `compaction_tokens_removed`, `model_latency_p50_ms`, `model_latency_p95_ms`, `idle_ms`, `retries_provider`.

215	Tool behavior (26 fields, all D, no council additions): `tool_calls`, `tool_calls_by_name{}`, `tool_errors`, `tool_error_rate`, `tool_timeouts`, `tool_aborts`, `shell_nonzero_exits`, `fs_reads`, `fs_writes`, `files_touched`, `diff_added_lines`, `diff_removed_lines`, `tests_run`, `tests_passed`, `lint_errors`, `type_errors`, `permission_requests`, `permission_denials`, `loop_hygiene_triggers`, `duplicate_tool_calls`, `longest_tool_ms`, `subagents_spawned`, `subagent_depth_max`, `workflow_agents_started`, `ralph_rounds`, `background_jobs`.
216	
217	Process quality (14 fields, D unless noted): `spec_present`, `spec_verdict_score` (S), `standard_authored_before_first_write`, `plan_present`, `plan_tasks`, `plan_tasks_completed`, `validator_authored_checks_ratio`, `read_barrier_violations`, `review_findings_total`, `review_findings_blocking`, `docs_updated`, `agent_note_present`, `snapshot_updated`, `coverage_delta`; the council added `structured_output_status`, `experiment_id`, `proposal_digest`, and `skill_loads[]`.
218	
219	Judge scores (10 fields, all S, cross-model, each with a confidence, no council additions): `correctness`, `robustness`, `code_quality`, `communication`, `spec_adherence`, `verification_rigor`, `efficiency_judgment`, `safety_compliance`, `overall`, `judge_disagreement`.
220	
221	Safety and oversight (6 fields, all D): `monitor_flags`, `high_impact_tool_calls`, `sandbox_violations`, `secrets_redacted`, `policy_overrides`, `human_interventions`; the council added `approval_records[]`, `decision_principals[]`, `dynamic_packages_mounted`, and `synthesized_in_play[]`.
222	
223	Training and data (10 fields, all D): `content_hash`, `dedupe_cluster_id`, `decontamination_status`, `redaction_applied`, `split`, `curriculum_difficulty`, `sample_weight`, `export_format_version`, `trainer_tokens`, `logprobs_available`; the council added `data_use_agreement_id`, `data_use_purposes[]`, `residency_region`, `redaction_profile_version`, `redaction_rule_hits`, `model_lineage_id`, `token_record_ref`, `provider_request_id_per_step[]` (all D), and `knowledge_scope` (S).
224	
225	The eight groups enumerate 136 original fields and 44 council additions, 180 in total; every D field must fold from a named session event or run report before it ships, per P2 above.
226	
227	## Alternatives considered
228	
229	**Best-only promotion.** An earlier design kept one merged head per generation and folded a losing variant back into nothing; every evaluated-but-unpromoted variant is now kept `alive` or `dominated` in a `dsh-archive` ledger, sampled for the next parent in proportion to quality × novelty × 1/(1+children) within islands per environment kind — Darwin Gödel Machine archive semantics, where low-scoring ancestors have proven necessary stepping stones toward the eventual best variant. This is rejected as the sole store because best-only hill-climbing has no stepping stones and no transparent lineage to audit for a fabricated result.
230	
231	**Self-selected evaluation cells.** An earlier design let the same proposal choose its own affected cells and predicted deltas before any run, and nothing froze the proposal before results were visible. This is rejected because it lets a semantic stage fund and shape its own evaluation; cells now derive from `SessionDiagnosis` evidence plus component lineage by a logged deterministic rule, and every proposal is content-hashed and frozen before a cell runs.
232	
233	**Reward computed in the implementer's workspace.** An earlier design ran checks against the same tree the implementer had just edited, so a certificate could pass because a test or a fixture was edited rather than because the task was solved. This is rejected because it is directly gameable — editing tests, `conftest.py`, or a package script earns a certificate — and reinforcement learning finds this exploit within tens of steps; checks now run on a pristine fixture plus the implementer's patch under `host` isolation with hidden checks, and a write under check-owned paths is a tamper verdict with reward zero.
234	
235	**Fleet sessions as reinforcement-learning data.** An earlier design for the model pipeline harvested fleet sessions directly for training, but a fleet session carries no environment identity, no group, and no seed, so decontamination, curriculum sampling, and GRPO grouping had nothing to key on. This is rejected in favor of an environment-first, group-first factory: the unit of data is a group of rollouts of one environment under one policy version produced by the runner on demand, and fleet sessions instead feed a short SFT cold start and the environment factory.
236	
237	**A single mutable knowledge store.** An earlier design called distilled skills, presets, and compositions "versioned plugins" but specified no digest, lineage, or generation identity for any of them, so a refined skill overwrote its prior body in place — a single mutable store under a plugin label, with no earlier generation to revert to and no way for a leaderboard to distinguish generations. This is rejected because lineage, decontamination, and rollback all need a stable identity per generation; every component and skill now carries a content-addressed id (`id@digest`) recorded in a log-only `CompositionManifest` event, and the `dsh-archive` ledger keeps every generation, retired ones included.
238	
239	**Judges as gates.** An earlier design let a council's verdict decide blocking outcomes directly in places without excluding judge transcripts from training by default, so a judge whose own prior verdicts could later train the model it judges would acquire a stake in its own future scoring. This is rejected because a same-lineage judge grading an outcome that affects it mislabels far more often than a disinterested one; judge sessions now carry a route distinct from the worker and validator lineage, every judge verdict is advisory until a D gate or a human decides, and judge transcripts default to exclusion from every training export.
240	
241	**Kept open: the artefact-lineage graph view.** An alternative representation draws nodes as durable records (a spec, a completion-standard revision, a certificate, a trajectory line, a dataset manifest, a model release) and edges as the sessions that produced one from another, with agents as edge labels rather than nodes; it makes "follow one artefact" and "diff two runs" native and turns W3 and W4's volumes into a Sankey diagram. It is not adopted here because it needs artefact ids the current schemas do not all carry yet (`SpecDraft`, `Plan`, and `SessionDiagnosis` have no stable identity of their own); it stays a candidate view once those ids exist.
242	
243	**Kept open: training on validator and judge role sessions.** Training the model on the roles its own pipeline needs — validator sessions that authored a standard matching the curated reference, diagnostician sessions, disinterested judge sessions — would let the model improve at those roles the way a verifier-first pipeline trains on its own generator and checker calls. It is not adopted here because judge transcripts default to exclusion from training so a judge never acquires a stake in its own verdicts; whether validator and diagnostician sessions specifically are safe to include is left to be decided per component lineage rather than fixed by this note.
244	
245	## Acceptance criteria
246	
247	### W1
248	
249	- The `environment/run` stamp and a `verification/run` event exist for every executed check, passing or failing, and a keyless test proves a certificate whose cited run is absent, has a different standard revision, or contains a failing check is rejected.
250	- `dsh-archive` records every evaluated `HarnessVariant` as `alive`, `dominated`, or `promoted`, never deletes a dominated entry, and a parent sampler draws from it in proportion to quality × novelty × 1/(1+children).
251	- A proposal from the quarantined Harness Engineer that touches an evaluator-owned path (`packages/improvement/**`, `packages/verification/**`, `scripts/run-gates.ts`, or a snapshot fixture) is a hard reject before any cell runs, proven by a fixture that submits such a patch.
252	- `@deepseek-ai/dsh-fleet` (`ctx.fleet`) runs a plan of environment × model × repetition cells through `ctx.environmentRuns` in a fresh workspace per cell, keeps a cell that cannot boot as `{ cell, error }` — a row with an error code, never a missing row — and folds a `LeaderboardRow` per model route and environment that never averages across `isolation` or `heldOut`; both stay columns a consumer partitions by. Its unit spec and its Loader-booted e2e (`examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/fleet-run`) already cover this.
253	- A model-visible text change produced by the loop — a mutated prompt section, tool schema, or skill body — cannot reach promotion without a human diff review of the re-recorded snapshot expectations.
254	
255	### W2
256	
257	- A keyless snapshot proves the read barrier: an implementer-role tool read under the standard's root is denied by fs policy while the same call from the validator succeeds, and a certificate from a session that composed a log-reading tool is rejected by invariant.
258	- `ProgramLedger` events map every goal of a program to its session, workspace, preset, isolation, budget, and status, and a Loader-booted example resumes a program from the ledger after a restart.
259	- A certificate's `treeHash` equals the merged head before a release record is generated; conflict resolution re-runs the checks rather than re-approving the per-goal certificates.
260	- A `signoff/recorded` event names the principal, the artefact hash, and the evidence in view for spec freeze, security or compliance relaxation, review acceptance, release, and training-data release, and none of these five transitions completes without one.
261	- The project's own checks enter training only after an `EnvironmentAdmission` record shows the pre-state failing, the reference passing, and a gaming-agent run failing to certify, plus a logged human split assignment.
262	
263	### W3
264	
265	- The `environment/run` stamp's content hashes of prompt, fixture, and checks are what a decontamination check keys on, and a fixture proves two runs of the same environment hash identically while a changed check hashes differently.
266	- A training run is refused if its reward did not originate from a `verification/run` event, and a fixture proves a write under check-owned paths of the pristine-fixture-plus-patch copy yields a tamper verdict with reward zero.
267	- Truncated, aborted, and errored rollouts are masked rather than scored as failures, proven by a fixture trajectory of each kind carrying no penalty in the training record.
268	- `EvalReport` pins the harness variant hash it ran under, and an evaluation on an unpinned variant is rejected as not comparable.
269	- A `ModelLineage` record generates the Article 53 documentation and the accountable officer's `SignoffRecord` before a `ModelRelease` exists.
270	
271	### W4
272	
273	- A `CompositionManifest` event names every component in play as `id@digest` at session start and on every preset, skill, or tool-set change, and an invariant rejects a skill result whose digest is absent from the manifest.
274	- A tier-1 skill candidate carries evidence sessions and a declared scope of session, department, or client, or is rejected by schema; the department scoreboard marks a skill deprecated only after paired present-versus-absent runs show a delta at or below zero over the configured number of runs.
275	- An `ExperimentPlan`'s proposal digest is logged before any of its cells run, and cells trace to `SessionDiagnosis` evidence plus a stratified sample by a logged deterministic rule, never to an S-set priority.
276	- The knowledge ledger's `id@digest` entries and the composition manifest's occurrences agree; a ledger entry with no matching manifest occurrence is flagged as never having been in play.
277	- Persisted artefacts are hash-chained per checkpoint and signed daily manifests reach write-once storage, and a per-client crypto-shredding key exists before any client-scoped erasure request can be honored.
278	
279	## Rollout
280	
281	1. **Landed** — the `environment/run` stamp, the `verification/run` event, and the runner that appends both: every executed run of a standard, passing or failing, is durable with its executor and workspace tree hash, a certificate needs a fully passing run of its revision, trajectories carry the attempt count, and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-fleet` (`ctx.fleet`) runs the cells and folds a leaderboard per route and environment. What remains of this item is the `EnvironmentStats` fold (pass@k per policy version) over the run events, which W1 stage 2 and W3 stage 2 read.
282	2. **Blocking** — the read barrier as filesystem and process authority. A validator-root fs-policy plugin, monotonic tool guards, implementer presets without a log-reading tool, and an invariant on certificates; until then every certificate measures only what the implementer could read.
283	3. **Blocking** — attributable decisions and pinned data-use terms. `signoff/recorded`, `decidedBy` with an argument digest on approvals, `dataUse/terms` at session creation, shipped redaction rules, and a curator that records rule hits; without them no client auditor can verify a gate and no transcript may become training data.
284	4. **Major** — content-addressed identity: component and skill digests, and the composition manifest event. Lineage, leaderboards per version, quarantine of dynamic packages, and the manifest-versus-ledger invariant all key on `id@digest`.
285	5. **Major** — scorekeeper as a session projection, and the archive ledger. `SessionFacts` folded beside goal and verification; `HarnessVariant` records over storage with parents, operators, evaluations, and status.
286	6. **Landed** — the budget policy plugin (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-budget-policy`): token, wall-time, and cost caps from config, folded from the session log on `agent/pre-step`, a `budget/breach` event, and a durable goal block no round driver resumes; the model sees nothing because the step never opens. What remains is wiring per-cell caps from the fleet plan.
287	7. **Major** — the experiment plugin: staged ladder, paired repetitions, bootstrap intervals, cost. Cells derived by rule, plans frozen and logged; the only place spend decisions live.
288	8. **Major** — structured output for top-level presets as a plugin. Attach the structured-output runtime to a preset's agent context; Intake, Program service, and Trajectory Analyst get forced schemas with logged rejection paths.
289	9. **Major** — trainer operator, model registry, model lineage, environment factory, and admission. W3 end to end, including the Article 53 documentation generated from the lineage record.
290	10. **Minor** — the deny-capable monitor on the tool guard. Impact classes deny by default, ask for a bounded class, and log `oversight/deny`; makes deployment and secrets human gates.
291	11. **Minor** — durable orchestration. Deferred: cells are idempotent by header hash × environment × repetition and recover from persisted child sessions; a journaling workflow engine provider arrives with the program ledger.
292	12. **Minor** — a live run viewer fed by session logs and workflow events. The client's `ui-workflow-run` renders run, phase, and member status only today; a model's-eye view at any seq is the view no competitor can prove complete.
293	
294	## Risks
295	
296	- **Oracle capture.** A patch author re-recording its own snapshot expectations turns a deterministic gate into a rubber stamp; only a human diff review of the recording route defends against it, and it is not automatic anywhere in these workflows.
297	- **Cheap reward under weak isolation.** Under `isolation: none`, checks run with the implementer's privileges in the implementer's own workspace, so a certificate there is not evidence a client or a trainer should treat as strong; leaderboards and training exports must partition by isolation, never blend it.
298	- **Survivorship in the fold.** A session that is skipped, torn by a restart, or interrupted mid-fan-out must still leave a scoreboard row carrying an error code; silently dropping it inflates every certificate rate computed from the remaining rows.
299	- **Data protection before export.** Redaction, consent, and residency events must exist and be enforced before any client transcript reaches an export; an export that runs ahead of the curator plugin and the pinned data-use terms is a confidentiality and residency incident, not a near-miss.
300	- **Judge and reviewer stake.** A judge or reviewer whose own verdicts could later train the model it grades, or whose approval volume is high enough to induce fatigue, degrades toward rubber-stamping; judge transcripts default to exclusion from training, and every human gate stays a named, attributed decision rather than an anonymous one.
301	- **Harness and model co-evolution.** Evaluating a model checkpoint on a harness that evolved against that same checkpoint's predecessor measures the pair, not either alone; `EvalReport` pins the harness variant hash for exactly this reason.
302	- **Orchestration loss.** Hours-long fan-outs run in-process today with no durable resume; without idempotent cells keyed by header hash × environment × repetition, a restart during a long fleet run or a long program double-counts or silently drops work.
303	- **Cost.** Role separation and staged evaluation spend more than a self-judging pipeline; per-goal and per-cell budgets from config, not code constants, are what keeps that cost bounded and visible.
304

1	/**
2	 * Pure projection of one session log into a {@link Trajectory}: surface
3	 * messages with their source seqs, per-step usage, the reward the log's goal
4	 * and verification events decide, and the components in play.
5	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-trajectories
6	 */
7	
8	import { ComponentId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-components'
9	import type { ComponentId as ComponentIdType } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-components/types'
10	import { decodeEnvironmentRun } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environments'
11	import type { EnvironmentRunStamp } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environments/types'
12	import { decodeGoalChange } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-goal'
13	import type { GoalSnapshot } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-goal/types'
14	import type { ContentBlock, ToolCallBlock } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
15	import { foldSurface } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
16	import type { EpochHeader, SessionEvent, SessionHeader } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
17	import { foldVerification } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-verification'
18	import type {
19	  Trajectory,
20	  TrajectoryMessage,
21	  TrajectoryReward,
22	  TrajectoryStep,
23	  TrajectoryToolCall,
24	} from './types.ts'
25	
26	/** The record format tag every exported line carries. */
27	export const TRAJECTORY_FORMAT = 'dsh-trajectory/1'
28	
29	/** Position of a surface event inside the turn/step structure. */
30	interface StepPosition {
31	  readonly turn: number
32	  readonly step: number
33	}
34	
35	/** Everything one sequential pass over the log collects before the surface is projected. */
36	interface LogScan {
37	  header?: EpochHeader
38	  agentPreset?: string
39	  environment?: EnvironmentRunStamp
40	  goal?: GoalSnapshot
41	  goalCompleted: boolean
42	  readonly positions: Map<number, StepPosition>
43	  readonly steps: TrajectoryStep[]
44	  readonly toolNames: string[]
45	}
46	
47	/**
48	 * Read the preset selection from a log-only event this package does not
49	 * declare. The event belongs to `dsh-agent-presets`; reading it by name keeps
50	 * the fold free of that dependency, and the payload check is the durable-log
51	 * boundary's own validation.
52	 */
53	function presetOf(event: SessionEvent): string | undefined {
54	  if ((event.type as string) !== 'agent-preset/selected') return undefined
55	  const data = event.data as { agentPreset?: unknown }
56	  return typeof data.agentPreset === 'string' ? data.agentPreset : undefined
57	}
58	
59	/** One ordered pass over every event, collecting what the projection needs. */
60	function scanLog(events: readonly SessionEvent[]): LogScan {
61	  const scan: LogScan = {
62	    goalCompleted: false,
63	    positions: new Map(),
64	    steps: [],
65	    toolNames: [],
66	  }
67	  let position: StepPosition | undefined
68	  for (const event of events) {
69	    switch (event.type) {
70	      case 'request/header':
71	        scan.header = event.data.header
72	        break
73	      case 'step/start':
74	        position = { turn: event.data.turn, step: event.data.step }
75	        scan.steps.push(position)
76	        break
77	      case 'step/end':
78	        position = undefined
79	        break
80	      case 'user/message':
81	      case 'tool/result':
82	        if (position !== undefined) scan.positions.set(event.seq, position)
83	        break
84	      case 'assistant/message': {
85	        if (position !== undefined) scan.positions.set(event.seq, position)
86	        const usage = event.data.usage
87	        if (usage !== undefined) {
88	          const index = scan.steps.findIndex(step => step.turn === event.data.turn && step.step === event.data.step)
89	          if (index !== -1) scan.steps[index] = { ...scan.steps[index] as TrajectoryStep, usage }
90	        }
91	        break
92	      }
93	      case 'tool/call':
94	        if (!scan.toolNames.includes(event.data.name)) scan.toolNames.push(event.data.name)
95	        break
96	      case 'goal/change': {
97	        const change = decodeGoalChange(event.data)
98	        if (change === undefined || change.operation === 'clear') break
99	        scan.goal = change.goal
100	        scan.goalCompleted = change.operation === 'complete'
101	        break
102	      }
103	      case 'environment/run': {
104	        // The durable boundary validates the stamp; a malformed one fails the fold loudly.
105	        const stamp = decodeEnvironmentRun(event.data)
106	        if (stamp !== undefined) scan.environment = stamp
107	        break
108	      }
109	      default: {
110	        const preset = presetOf(event)
111	        if (preset !== undefined) scan.agentPreset = preset
112	      }
113	    }
114	  }
115	  return scan
116	}
117	
118	/** Tool calls an assistant message requested, from its own blocks. */
119	function toolCallsOf(content: readonly ContentBlock[]): TrajectoryToolCall[] {
120	  return content
121	    .filter((block): block is ToolCallBlock => block.type === 'tool-call')
122	    .map(block => ({ id: block.id, name: block.name, arguments: block.arguments }))
123	}
124	
125	/** Project one surface event to a trajectory message, or nothing for an empty assistant step. */
126	function projectMessage(event: SessionEvent, position: StepPosition | undefined): TrajectoryMessage | undefined {
127	  const at = position === undefined ? {} : { turn: position.turn, step: position.step }
128	  switch (event.type) {
129	    case 'user/message':
130	      return { role: 'user', seq: event.seq, ...at, content: event.data.content, sourceKind: event.data.source.kind }
131	    case 'assistant/message': {
132	      const message = event.data.message
133	      if (message.content.length === 0) return undefined
134	      const toolCalls = toolCallsOf(message.content)
135	      return {
136	        role: 'assistant',
137	        seq: event.seq,
138	        ...at,
139	        content: message.content,
140	        sourceKind: message.source.kind,
141	        ...toolCalls.length === 0 ? {} : { toolCalls },
142	      }
143	    }
144	    case 'tool/result': {
145	      const [block] = event.data.message.content
146	      return {
147	        role: 'tool',
148	        seq: event.seq,
149	        ...at,
150	        content: block.content,
151	        sourceKind: event.data.message.source.kind,
152	        toolCallId: block.toolCallId,
153	        ...block.isError === true ? { isError: true } : {},
154	      }
155	    }
156	    /* v8 ignore next 2 -- the surface fold admits only the three message-producing types. */
157	    default:
158	      return undefined
159	  }
160	}
161	
162	/** Decide the reward from the goal and the verification fold. */
163	function decideReward(scan: LogScan, events: readonly SessionEvent[]): TrajectoryReward {
164	  const verification = foldVerification(events)
165	  const goal = scan.goal === undefined
166	    ? {}
167	    : { goal: { id: scan.goal.id, objective: scan.goal.objective, phase: scan.goal.phase } }
168	  const counts = {
169	    directives: verification.directivesIssued,
170	    relaxations: verification.standard?.relaxed.length ?? 0,
171	    attempts: verification.runsRecorded,
172	  }
173	  if (verification.standard !== undefined) {
174	    return verification.certificate === undefined
175	      ? { outcome: 0, basis: 'certificate', ...goal, ...counts }
176	      : { outcome: 1, basis: 'certificate', ...goal, certificate: verification.certificate, ...counts }
177	  }
178	  if (scan.goalCompleted) return { outcome: null, basis: 'uncertified-completion', ...goal, ...counts }
179	  return { outcome: null, basis: 'none', ...goal, ...counts }
180	}
181	
182	/** Component ids in play, in the component registry's id scheme. */
183	function componentsOf(scan: LogScan): ComponentIdType[] {
184	  const ids: string[] = []
185	  if (scan.agentPreset !== undefined) ids.push(`composition:${scan.agentPreset}`)
186	  if (scan.environment !== undefined) ids.push(`environment:${scan.environment.environmentId}`)
187	  if (scan.header !== undefined) ids.push(`model-provider:${scan.header.config.provider}`)
188	  for (const name of scan.toolNames) ids.push(`tool:${name}`)
189	  return ids.map(ComponentId)
190	}
191	
192	/**
193	 * Fold one session into its trajectory.
194	 * @param meta - the session header.
195	 * @param events - the session's contiguous event log.
196	 * @returns the trajectory; deterministic for the same inputs.
197	 */
198	export function foldTrajectory(meta: SessionHeader, events: readonly SessionEvent[]): Trajectory {
199	  const scan = scanLog(events)
200	  const bySeq = new Map(events.map(event => [event.seq, event] as const))
201	  const messages: TrajectoryMessage[] = []
202	  for (const seq of foldSurface(events).nodes) {
203	    const event = bySeq.get(seq)
204	    /* v8 ignore next -- surface nodes cite seqs of the log they were folded from. */
205	    if (event === undefined) continue
206	    const message = projectMessage(event, scan.positions.get(seq))
207	    if (message !== undefined) messages.push(message)
208	  }
209	  const reward = decideReward(scan, events)
210	  const header = scan.header
211	  return {
212	    format: TRAJECTORY_FORMAT,
213	    id: meta.id,
214	    source: {
215	      sessionId: meta.id,
216	      createdAt: meta.createdAt,
217	      ...meta.cwd === undefined ? {} : { cwd: meta.cwd },
218	      ...meta.parentSession === undefined ? {} : { parentSession: meta.parentSession },
219	      ...scan.agentPreset === undefined ? {} : { agentPreset: scan.agentPreset },
220	    },
221	    ...scan.environment === undefined ? {} : { environment: scan.environment },
222	    ...header === undefined ? {} : { config: header.config },
223	    ...header?.system === undefined ? {} : { system: header.system },
224	    ...header?.tools === undefined ? {} : { tools: header.tools },
225	    messages,
226	    steps: scan.steps,
227	    reward,
228	    provenance: {
229	      components: componentsOf(scan),
230	      toolNames: scan.toolNames,
231	      ...reward.certificate === undefined ? {} : { isolation: reward.certificate.isolation },
232	    },
233	  }
234	}

1	/**
2	 * Trajectory export: persisted sessions folded into `dsh-trajectory/1`
3	 * records and written one JSON line at a time to a caller-supplied sink. The
4	 * service reads through the session persistence seam and writes no session
5	 * event. The
6	 * [trajectory-export Agent Note](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-trajectory-export-and-environment-registry.md)
7	 * owns the design rationale.
8	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-trajectories
9	 */
10	
11	import { open } from 'node:fs/promises'
12	import { Context, Service } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
13	// Type-only: resolves ctx.sessionPersistence.
14	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-persistence'
15	import { foldTrajectory } from './fold.ts'
16	import type {
17	  TrajectoryExportReport,
18	  TrajectoryExportRequest,
19	  TrajectoryExportSkip,
20	  TrajectorySink,
21	} from './types.ts'
22	
23	export type * from './types.ts'

32	/** Render a read or fold failure for the export report without trusting the thrown value. */
33	function reasonOf(error: unknown): string {
34	  return error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)
35	}

37	/**
38	 * A sink that appends lines to one file, created or truncated on first use.
39	 * @param path - destination file path.
40	 * @returns a sink the exporter closes when the export settles.
41	 */
42	export function jsonlFileSink(path: string): TrajectorySink {
43	  const handle = open(path, 'w')
44	  return {
45	    async write(line) {
46	      await (await handle).write(line)
47	    },
48	    async close() {
49	      await (await handle).close()
50	    },
51	  }

54	/** Trajectory exporter (`ctx.trajectories`): persisted sessions as training and evaluation records. */
55	export class TrajectoryService extends Service {
56	  static inject = ['sessionPersistence']
57	
58	  constructor(ctx: Context) {
59	    super(ctx, 'trajectories')
60	  }
61	
62	  /**
63	   * Fold the requested sessions and write one line per trajectory. A session
64	   * that cannot be read or folded is reported and the export continues; the
65	   * sink is closed exactly once when every session has been handled.
66	   * @param request - sessions to export, the destination sink, the reward filter, and the held-out opt-in.
67	   * @returns counts of sessions, written lines, rewarded lines, filtered sessions, withheld held-out sessions, and skips with reasons.
68	   */
69	  async export(request: TrajectoryExportRequest): Promise<TrajectoryExportReport> {
70	    const persistence = this.ctx.sessionPersistence
71	    const sessions = request.sessions ?? (await persistence.list()).map(header => header.id)
72	    const skipped: TrajectoryExportSkip[] = []
73	    let exported = 0
74	    let rewarded = 0
75	    let filtered = 0
76	    let heldOut = 0
77	    try {
78	      for (const sessionId of sessions) {
79	        let line: string
80	        let outcome: 1 | 0 | null
81	        let reserved: boolean
82	        try {
83	          const { meta, events } = await persistence.inspect(sessionId)
84	          const trajectory = foldTrajectory(meta, events)
85	          outcome = trajectory.reward.outcome
86	          reserved = trajectory.environment?.heldOut === true
87	          line = `${JSON.stringify(trajectory)}\n`
88	        } catch (error: unknown) {
89	          skipped.push({ sessionId, reason: reasonOf(error) })
90	          continue
91	        }
92	        if (reserved && request.includeHeldOut !== true) {
93	          heldOut += 1
94	          continue
95	        }
96	        if (request.rewardedOnly === true && outcome !== 1) {
97	          filtered += 1
98	          continue
99	        }
100	        await request.sink.write(line)
101	        exported += 1
102	        if (outcome === 1) rewarded += 1
103	      }
104	    } finally {
105	      await request.sink.close()
106	    }
107	    return { sessions: sessions.length, exported, rewarded, filtered, heldOut, skipped }
108	  }
109	}

118	  readonly format: TrajectoryFormat
119	  /** Trajectory identity, the session id. */
120	  readonly id: SessionId
121	  readonly source: TrajectorySource
122	  /** The environment the session ran, from its `environment/run` stamp; absent for a session no runner stamped. */
123	  readonly environment?: EnvironmentRunStamp
124	  /** Call configuration of the last logged request header, absent for a session that made no request. */

129	  readonly tools?: readonly ToolSchema[]
130	  /** Model-visible messages in surface order. */
131	  readonly messages: readonly TrajectoryMessage[]
132	  /** Model calls in log order. */
133	  readonly steps: readonly TrajectoryStep[]
134	  readonly reward: TrajectoryReward
135	  readonly provenance: TrajectoryProvenance

138	/** Destination of exported lines; the exporter closes it when the export settles. */
139	export interface TrajectorySink {
140	  /**
141	   * Accept one complete line, newline included.
142	   * @param line - one serialized trajectory followed by `\n`.

144	  write(line: string): Promise<void> | void
145	  /** Release the destination; called exactly once, after the last write or after a failure. */
146	  close(): Promise<void> | void
147	}
148	
149	/** What to export and where. */
150	export interface TrajectoryExportRequest {
151	  /** Sessions to export; absent exports every persisted session. */
152	  readonly sessions?: readonly SessionId[]
153	  /** Destination of the lines. */
154	  readonly sink: TrajectorySink
155	  /** Write only trajectories whose reward outcome is `1`. */
156	  readonly rewardedOnly?: boolean
157	  /** Also write sessions whose environment is held out; absent withholds them, so evaluation tasks never train by default. */
158	  readonly includeHeldOut?: boolean

165	  readonly reason: string

169	export interface TrajectoryExportReport {
170	  /** Sessions the request named or the store listed. */
171	  readonly sessions: number

173	  readonly exported: number
174	  /** Written lines whose reward outcome is `1`. */
175	  readonly rewarded: number
176	  /** Readable sessions withheld by `rewardedOnly`. */
177	  readonly filtered: number
178	  /** Readable sessions withheld because their environment is held out. */
179	  readonly heldOut: number

# AGENTS.md — Harness Packages

These package-specific rules supplement the repo-wide [conventions](../AGENTS.md#conventions).

- **Plugin exports:** service packages default-export their service class; function plugins named-export `name` / `inject` / `Config` / `apply` and have no default export. Mixing the forms makes the Loader discard the function plugin's namespace ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **Optional services use `ctx.get(name)`.** Reserve `ctx.<name>` for declared injections; the property proxy is topology-sensitive, while strict `ctx.get` reads the global service store ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **Product-visible plugins require a non-unit REAL-composition test.** Hand-built `ctx.plugin(...)` suites are insufficient. Boot test-only `cordis.yml` through the Loader and app/process; mock only external services or nondeterministic inputs and assert model-visible, durable, or user-visible output. Keep opt-ins out of shipped defaults. [Policy](../docs/testing.md).
- **Initiator-owned private chains derive, then capture.** Under `ctx.agents.withInitiator()`, recover the Agent at each orchestration entry, derive `agent.session`, and let operation-local helpers close over it. Keep `Agent` and `Session` explicit at lifecycle, session-log, service, authority, worker/process, persistence, and wire interfaces; do not widen a leaf helper from `Session` to `Context` merely to hide a parameter ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-15-agent-initiator-scope.md)).
- **Represent one asynchronous operation with one lifecycle controller or transaction.** Separate readiness, cancellation, disposal, reservation, or sentinel state requires an independent owner or settlement point; otherwise fold it while preserving rollback, callback containment, and quiescence.
- **Design Service Definitions for all current Consumers.** Keep tool-schema, Loader, UI, transport, and provider-specific behavior in the Consumer or provider; do not let one Consumer dictate the service contract ([capability-seam rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-06-13-capability-seams.md)). Inverse smell: a public service method with one internal caller — pass a private capability closure instead (`RunCodeBridgeOptions`).
- **Require a current owner and need.** Tie each abstraction, state machine, option, defensive copy, and compatibility path to a current contract or production consumer, and keep behavior in its owning plugin or service.
- **Require evidence for public choices.** Configurability does not justify an unsupported default, public operation set, format, or imported external concept. Use current-consumer evidence or relevant prior art; otherwise require an explicit value or defer the choice.
- **Write model-facing contracts from the model's perspective.** Prompts, tool schemas, results, and diagnostics contain only task-relevant concepts, not UI, transport, or implementation vocabulary. Pin stable model-visible text verbatim and dynamic behavior through snapshots or end-to-end coverage.
- **Enforce a decision in the operation that makes it.** Schema omission, prompt filtering, facades, wrappers, and listener order are not enforcement when direct or alternate callers can bypass them; test denial through the executor.
- **Publish state only at its commit point.** Emit each notification and update derived state only after the operation succeeds; derive caches, prompts, UI echoes, replay, and query views from one authoritative source.
- **Apply bounds to the complete result.** Enforce byte, token, item, and time limits where the complete emitted or retained value, including wrappers and metadata, is known; test tiny and exact limits, oversized single chunks, and multibyte byte limits.
- **Registry contributions prove disposal** through the HMR-safety test required by [testing policy](../docs/testing.md): dispose the fiber and observe removal.
- **Every package owns `./invariant`.** Register the manifest name; check an event/data relation or give empty installers package-specific `No runtime invariant:` reasons. Generated companions, unexplained empties, and ignored reporters fail [`verify-package-invariants`](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-19-package-invariant-runtime-contracts.md).

[Naming rules](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md#name-the-role-that-exists):

- **Package tsconfig:** extends `tsconfig.base.json` (Client: `tsconfig.base.client.json`), uses `rootDir: src`, `outDir: lib/types`, and references each workspace dependency plus `runtime-diagnostics/invariants`; registers in exactly one aggregate. Only `api/remotes` splits for generated contracts; ordinary two-entry Client plugins do not ([layout](../docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- `src/types.ts` contains only types — no runtime code.
- Tests live at package level under `tests/`, not `src/__tests__/`.
- A package's README and JSDoc are part of the change: altered behavior (config keys, defaults, error codes, wire fields) updates them in the same commit. `doc-sync` gates what it can; apply [dsh-prose-standard](../.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for complete, concise prose and verify accuracy against code.
- Package READMEs document model, token, and KV-cache effects using the [canonical Model Experience format](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md#4-write-the-package-readme).
- Package READMEs put durable consumer gaps and non-obvious maintainer constraints under `## Known Limitations and Deferred Work`; ordinary cleanup stays in its TODO or Agent Note. Packages with none use a justified [allowlist entry](../scripts/verify-package-readme-limitations.ts) ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-10-readme-known-limitations-gate.md)).

1	/**
2	 * Pure types of a fleet run: the plan, the cells, each cell's outcome, and the
3	 * leaderboard rows folded from the outcomes, free of host-side imports.
4	 *
5	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-fleet/types
6	 */
7	
8	import type { EnvironmentRunReport } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environment-runner/types'
9	import type { EnvironmentFilter, EnvironmentId, EnvironmentRunModel } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environments/types'
10	import type { CertificateIsolation } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-verification/types'
11	
12	/** Which environments a plan runs: named ids, or everything the registry filter matches. */
13	export type FleetEnvironmentSelection =
14	  | { readonly ids: readonly EnvironmentId[] }
15	  | { readonly filter: EnvironmentFilter }
16	
17	/** One fleet run: every selected environment on every model route, `repetitions` times. */
18	export interface FleetPlan {
19	  /** Environments to run. */
20	  readonly environments: FleetEnvironmentSelection
21	  /** Model routes; an empty list runs the composition's default route. */
22	  readonly models: readonly EnvironmentRunModel[]
23	  /** Positive number of repetitions per environment and model; repetition indexes start at zero. */
24	  readonly repetitions: number
25	  /** Existing absolute directory under which every cell gets its own fresh workspace directory. */
26	  readonly workspaceRoot: string
27	  /** Batch identity written into every run stamp as `group`; absent mints one. */
28	  readonly group?: string
29	  /** Aborts the remaining cells when it fires; started cells abort through the runner. */
30	  readonly signal?: AbortSignal
31	}
32	
33	/** One environment × model × repetition unit of a plan. */
34	export interface FleetCell {
35	  readonly environment: EnvironmentId
36	  readonly model: EnvironmentRunModel
37	  readonly repetition: number
38	}
39	
40	/** What one cell produced: the runner's report, or the failure that prevented one. */
41	export type FleetCellOutcome =
42	  | { readonly cell: FleetCell; readonly report: EnvironmentRunReport }
43	  | { readonly cell: FleetCell; readonly error: FleetCellError }
44	
45	/** A cell that produced no report; the code is the thrown harness error's when it had one. */
46	export interface FleetCellError {
47	  readonly code?: string
48	  readonly message: string
49	}
50	
51	/**
52	 * One leaderboard row: one model route on one environment. Rows are never
53	 * averaged across isolation levels or across the held-out split; both are
54	 * columns a consumer partitions by.
55	 */
56	export interface LeaderboardRow {
57	  readonly provider: string
58	  readonly model: string
59	  readonly environmentId: EnvironmentId
60	  readonly environmentKind: string
61	  readonly heldOut: boolean

75	  readonly inputTokens: number

1	/**
2	 * Pure types of the environment domain: identities, the merge-extensible kind
3	 * map, and the task-with-verifiers definition, free of host-side imports.
4	 *
5	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-environments/types
6	 */
7	
8	import type { Branded } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-brand'
9	import type { CertificateIsolation, StandardCheck } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-verification/types'
10	
11	/** Identifies one environment across compositions; derived from its producer's stable name, never from mount order. */
12	export type EnvironmentId = Branded<'EnvironmentId'>
13	
14	/**
15	 * Merge-extensible map from environment kind to that kind's detail type. Each
16	 * producer package declares its kind by declaration merging; the registry
17	 * itself ships no kind.
18	 */
19	export interface EnvironmentKindMap {}
20	
21	/** Every declared environment kind; `string` while no producer has merged a kind into the program. */
22	export type EnvironmentKind = [keyof EnvironmentKindMap] extends [never] ? string : Extract<keyof EnvironmentKindMap, string>
23	
24	/** Kind-specific detail declared by the kind's producer; `unknown` for kinds outside this program. */
25	export type EnvironmentDetail<K extends string> = K extends keyof EnvironmentKindMap ? EnvironmentKindMap[K] : unknown
26	
27	/** Whether people curated an environment or an agent synthesized it. */
28	export type EnvironmentProvenance = 'curated' | 'synthesized'
29	
30	/** The work an environment asks of an agent. */

205	        // the versioned contract says the cached state shape differs, so the
206	        // two registrants cannot share cells. Anything else about a definition
207	        // is functions, which no runtime comparison can tell apart.
208	        if (existing.def.stateVersion !== definition.stateVersion) {
209	          throw new Error(`session projection key ${JSON.stringify(key)} is already registered at stateVersion ${String(existing.def.stateVersion)}; refusing to share it with stateVersion ${String(definition.stateVersion)}`)
210	        }
211	        existing.refs += 1
212	      }
213	      yield () => {
214	        const live = this.registrations.get(key)
215	        /* v8 ignore next -- the disposer runs once per successful registration, so the entry it counted is still here */
216	        if (live === undefined) return
217	        live.refs -= 1
218	        if (live.refs === 0) this.registrations.delete(key)
219	      }
220	    }.bind(this), 'sessionProjections.register()')
221	    return () => void dispose()
222	  }
223	
224	  /**
225	   * Subscribe to the change feed. The registration is an effect on the
226	   * calling context's fiber.
227	   * @param listener - called once per unit whose state reference changed, per committed event.
228	   * @returns the exact disposer that unsubscribes.
229	   */
230	  onChanged(listener: ProjectionChangeListener): () => void {
231	    const dispose = this.ctx.effect(() => {
232	      this.listeners.add(listener)
233	      return () => {
234	        this.listeners.delete(listener)
235	      }
236	    }, 'sessionProjections.onChanged()')
237	    return () => void dispose()
238	  }
239	
240	  /**
241	   * One consistent cut over every registered unit for one session, read from
242	   * the watermark cache (missing cells fold lazily over the in-memory log).
243	   * Fully synchronous — every value and `asOfSeq` reflect the same log
244	   * position. Each value passes its unit's schema before leaving.
245	   * @param session - the session whose projection values are read.
246	   * @returns the snapshot; `values` is empty when no unit is registered.
247	   */
248	  snapshot(session: Session): ProjectionSnapshot {
249	    const values: Record<string, unknown> = {}
250	    for (const registration of this.registrations.values()) {
251	      const cell = this.cellFor(registration, session)
252	      values[registration.def.key] = registration.def.schema.parse(registration.def.view(cell.state))
253	    }
254	    return { asOfSeq: session.seq - 1, values: values }
255	  }
256	
257	  /**
258	   * State-level checkpoint of every registered unit for one session, read
259	   * from the watermark cache (missing cells fold lazily over the in-memory
260	   * log). This is the write side of the persisted projection cache: the
261	   * returned rows are the `(key → {ver, seq, val})` part of the durable
262	   * `(sessionId, key, ver, seq, val)`
263	   * rows. Every `val` is a DETACHED structured clone — never the live
264	   * cell reference: the watermark cache is this registry's authoritative
265	   * mutable state, and a caller reaching the live reference could corrupt
266	   * every subsequent snapshot and frame through it (plain JSON by the unit
267	   * contract, so the clone is total).
268	   * @param session - the session whose unit states are checkpointed.
269	   * @returns one row per registered key; empty when no unit is registered.
270	   */
271	  checkpoint(session: Session): ProjectionCheckpoint {
272	    const rows: ProjectionCheckpoint = {}
273	    for (const registration of this.registrations.values()) {
274	      const cell = this.cellFor(registration, session)
275	      rows[registration.def.key] = {
276	        ver: registration.def.stateVersion,
277	        seq: cell.observedSeq,
278	        val: structuredClone(cell.state),
279	      }
280	    }
281	    return rows
282	  }
283	
284	  /**
285	   * The stored seq a {@link restore} tail read over `checkpoint` must start
286	   * at: one event BELOW the lowest usable watermark (a row is usable when
287	   * its `ver` matches the live unit's `stateVersion`; an absent or mismatched row
288	   * pulls the floor to `0` — that key must refold the full log). The
289	   * one-below anchor is load-bearing: the tail then proves how far the
290	   * stored log still extends, so {@link restore} can detect a log that
291	   * shrank below a row's watermark (crash-repair truncation) instead of
292	   * serving the stale row as current — an empty tail read from the anchor
293	   * yields an end below every watermark and the restore rejects for a full
294	   * re-read.
295	   * @param checkpoint - persisted rows for one session (possibly stale or empty).
296	   * @returns the seq to hand the persistence `readFrom`, or `undefined`
297	   *   when no unit is registered (no read needed — {@link restore} would
298	   *   serve empty values regardless).
299	   */
300	  restoreFloor(checkpoint: ProjectionCheckpoint): number | undefined {
301	    let floor: number | undefined
302	    for (const registration of this.registrations.values()) {
303	      const row = checkpoint[registration.def.key]
304	      const need = row !== undefined && row.ver === registration.def.stateVersion
305	        ? Math.max(row.seq + 1, 0)
306	        : 0
307	      floor = floor === undefined ? need : Math.min(floor, need)
308	    }
309	    return floor === undefined ? undefined : Math.max(floor - 1, 0)
310	  }
311	
312	  /**
313	   * View a checkpoint's rows without any log read: for every registered
314	   * unit whose row's `ver` matches, serve the schema-validated
315	   * `view` of the stored state; mismatched or absent rows leave their key
316	   * absent (a cold or listing consumer treats it as not-yet-available and a
317	   * fuller read path refolds it). The zero-I/O rung of the read ladder —
318	   * values are as stale as their rows, never wrong.
319	   * @param checkpoint - persisted rows for one session (possibly stale or empty).
320	   * @returns whole values per key with a usable row; empty when none.
321	   */
322	  viewCheckpoint(checkpoint: ProjectionCheckpoint): Partial<SessionProjectionMap> {
323	    const values: Record<string, unknown> = {}
324	    for (const registration of this.registrations.values()) {
325	      const def = registration.def
326	      const row = checkpoint[def.key]
327	      if (row === undefined || row.ver !== def.stateVersion) continue
328	      values[def.key] = def.schema.parse(def.view(row.val))
329	    }
330	    return values
331	  }
332	
333	  /**
334	   * Cold read: fold every registered unit over a stored log suffix, seeding
335	   * each from its checkpoint row when usable — the one read recipe (cached
336	   * state + forward tail replay + `view`) applied without a live `Session`.
337	   * Call with the events returned by a persistence
338	   * `readFrom(id, restoreFloor(checkpoint))` and that same floor as
339	   * `baseSeq`; the floor's one-below anchor makes the supplied end honest,
340	   * so a shrunk log is detected here. A row is usable iff its
341	   * `ver` matches the live unit's `stateVersion`, it does not predate `baseSeq`
342	   * (`seq >= baseSeq - 1`), and it does not claim events past the
343	   * supplied end (`seq <= endSeq`); an unusable row is discarded
344	   * and its key refolds from `init` — which is only sound over the full
345	   * log, so a discarded row with `baseSeq > 0` throws (the caller re-reads
346	   * from seq 0, e.g. after a crash-repair truncation shrank the log below
347	   * a row's watermark).
348	   * @param checkpoint - persisted rows for one session (possibly stale or empty).
349	   * @param events - the stored events with `seq >= baseSeq`, in seq order.
350	   * @param baseSeq - the seq `events` starts at (its first event's seq when non-empty).
351	   * @returns the snapshot cut at the supplied log end (`asOfSeq` is the last
352	   *   supplied event's seq, `baseSeq - 1` for an empty tail) plus the
353	   *   refreshed checkpoint rows at that cut, ready for a durable write-back.
354	   */
355	  restore(checkpoint: ProjectionCheckpoint, events: readonly SessionEvent[], baseSeq: number):
356	  { snapshot: ProjectionSnapshot; checkpoint: ProjectionCheckpoint } {
357	    const endSeq = events.at(-1)?.seq ?? baseSeq - 1
358	    const values: Record<string, unknown> = {}
359	    const refreshed: ProjectionCheckpoint = {}
360	    for (const registration of this.registrations.values()) {
361	      const def = registration.def
362	      const row = checkpoint[def.key]
363	      const usable = row !== undefined
364	        && row.ver === def.stateVersion
365	        && row.seq >= baseSeq - 1
366	        && row.seq <= endSeq
367	      if (!usable && baseSeq > 0) {
368	        throw new Error(
369	          `session projection ${JSON.stringify(def.key)} cannot restore from seq ${baseSeq}: `
370	          + 'its checkpoint row is missing, version-mismatched, or beyond the supplied log end; re-read from seq 0',
371	        )
372	      }
373	      let state = usable ? row.val : def.init()
374	      const from = usable ? row.seq : baseSeq - 1
375	      for (const event of events) {
376	        if (event.seq > from) state = def.apply(state, event)
377	      }
378	      values[def.key] = def.schema.parse(def.view(state))
379	      refreshed[def.key] = { ver: def.stateVersion, seq: endSeq, val: state }
380	    }
381	    return {
382	      snapshot: { asOfSeq: endSeq, values: values },
383	      checkpoint: refreshed,
384	    }
385	  }
386	
387	  /** Fold one unit from init over `events`, producing a cell watermarked at the last folded event. */
388	  private buildCell(def: ErasedDefinition, events: readonly SessionEvent[]): UnitCell {
389	    let state = def.init()
390	    for (const event of events) state = def.apply(state, event)
391	    return { state, observedSeq: (events.at(-1)?.seq ?? -1) }
392	  }
393	
394	  /** Read (or lazily build, folding the full in-memory log) one unit's cell. */
395	  private cellFor(registration: Registration, session: Session): UnitCell {
396	    let cell = registration.cells.get(session)
397	    if (cell === undefined) {
398	      cell = this.buildCell(registration.def, session.events)
399	      registration.cells.set(session, cell)
400	    }
401	    return cell
402	  }
403	
404	  /** Eager drive: pass one committed event through every registered unit; notify on changed references. */
405	  private drive(session: Session, event: SessionEvent): void {
406	    for (const registration of this.registrations.values()) {
407	      let cell = registration.cells.get(session)
408	      if (cell === undefined) {
409	        // Late build mid-stream: fold history before this event (seq = log
410	        // index, so the prefix slice is exact), then take the normal gate.
411	        cell = this.buildCell(registration.def, session.events.slice(0, event.seq))
412	        registration.cells.set(session, cell)
413	      }
414	      const next = registration.def.apply(cell.state, event)
415	      const changed = !Object.is(next, cell.state)
416	      cell.state = next
417	      cell.observedSeq = event.seq
418	      if (changed && this.listeners.size > 0) {
419	        const value = registration.def.schema.parse(registration.def.view(next))
420	        for (const listener of this.listeners) {
421	          listener(session, registration.def.key as Extract<keyof SessionProjectionMap, string>, value, event.seq)
422	        }
423	      }
424	    }
425	  }
426	}

1	/**
2	 * Pure folds for durable provider-reported token usage and context occupancy.
3	 */
4	
5	import { z } from 'zod'
6	import type { TokenUsage } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
7	import type { SessionEvent } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
8	import type { ProjectionDefinition } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-projection'
9	import type { ContextPressureProjection, TokenUsageProjection } from './projection.ts'
10	import { foldSurfaceProjection } from './surface-projection.ts'
11	import type { ShadowPriceClaim } from './surface-projection.ts'
12	
13	interface UsageSample {
14	  turn: number
15	  step: number
16	  buckets: TokenUsageProjection
17	}
18	
19	interface TokenUsageState {
20	  totals: TokenUsageProjection
21	  last: UsageSample | null
22	}
23	
24	const zeroBuckets = (): TokenUsageProjection => ({
25	  uncachedInputTokens: 0,
26	  outputTokens: 0,
27	  cacheReadTokens: 0,
28	  cacheWriteTokens: 0,
29	})
30	
31	const bucketsFrom = (usage: TokenUsage): TokenUsageProjection => ({
32	  uncachedInputTokens: usage.inputTokens,
33	  outputTokens: usage.outputTokens,
34	  cacheReadTokens: usage.cacheReadTokens ?? 0,
35	  cacheWriteTokens: usage.cacheWriteTokens ?? 0,
36	})
37	
38	const bucketsEqual = (left: TokenUsageProjection, right: TokenUsageProjection): boolean =>
39	  left.uncachedInputTokens === right.uncachedInputTokens
40	  && left.outputTokens === right.outputTokens
41	  && left.cacheReadTokens === right.cacheReadTokens
42	  && left.cacheWriteTokens === right.cacheWriteTokens
43	
44	const addReplacing = (
45	  totals: TokenUsageProjection,
46	  previous: TokenUsageProjection | undefined,
47	  next: TokenUsageProjection,
48	): TokenUsageProjection => ({
49	  uncachedInputTokens: totals.uncachedInputTokens - (previous?.uncachedInputTokens ?? 0) + next.uncachedInputTokens,
50	  outputTokens: totals.outputTokens - (previous?.outputTokens ?? 0) + next.outputTokens,
51	  cacheReadTokens: totals.cacheReadTokens - (previous?.cacheReadTokens ?? 0) + next.cacheReadTokens,
52	  cacheWriteTokens: totals.cacheWriteTokens - (previous?.cacheWriteTokens ?? 0) + next.cacheWriteTokens,
53	})
54	
55	const projectionSchema = z.object({
56	  uncachedInputTokens: z.number().int().nonnegative(),
57	  outputTokens: z.number().int().nonnegative(),
58	  cacheReadTokens: z.number().int().nonnegative(),
59	  cacheWriteTokens: z.number().int().nonnegative(),
60	}).strict()
61	
62	// Cast for the optional values: under exactOptionalPropertyTypes zod infers
63	// `number | undefined` where the interface declares absent-or-number fields.
64	const pressureSchema = z.object({
65	  pressureTokens: z.number().int().nonnegative().optional(),
66	  projectedTokens: z.number().int().nonnegative().optional(),
67	  contextWindow: z.number().int().positive().optional(),
68	}).strict() as unknown as z.ZodType<ContextPressureProjection>
69	
70	/** Prompt-side pressure of one request: input plus cache traffic, no output. */
71	const pressureFrom = (usage: TokenUsage): number =>
72	  usage.inputTokens + (usage.cacheReadTokens ?? 0) + (usage.cacheWriteTokens ?? 0)
73	
74	/** The usage a chunk or finalized message reports for its step, if any. */
75	const usageOf = (event: SessionEvent): TokenUsage | undefined =>
76	  event.type === 'assistant/chunk' && event.data.chunk.type === 'usage'
77	    ? event.data.chunk.usage
78	    : event.type === 'assistant/message'
79	      ? event.data.usage
80	      : undefined
81	
82	/**
83	 * Context-occupancy state: the two independent last-wins records plus the
84	 * O(1) running surface total needed to carry the newest sample forward.
85	 */
86	interface ContextPressureState {
87	  contextWindow?: number
88	  pressureTokens?: number
89	  /** Running heuristic total over the current surface ({@link foldSurfaceProjection}). */
90	  surfaceTokens: number
91	  /** {@link surfaceTokens} at the newest usage sample; absent until one lands. */
92	  sampledSurfaceTokens?: number
93	  /** Shadow price armed by the immediately preceding metering event. */
94	  claim?: ShadowPriceClaim
95	}
96	
97	/**
98	 * Token-meter's session projection unit.
99	 *
100	 * Usage chunks provide an early sample that survives a later request failure;
101	 * an assistant message provides the final sample for the same turn/step. A
102	 * repeated sample replaces that step's earlier value instead of double
103	 * counting it. The single `last` slot relies on the session-log invariant
104	 * that usage reports for one turn/step are adjacent: once a later step begins,
105	 * a legal log never reports usage for an earlier step again.
106	 */
107	export const tokenUsageProjectionDefinition:
108	ProjectionDefinition<'tokenUsage', TokenUsageState> = {
109	  key: 'tokenUsage',
110	  schema: projectionSchema,
111	  init: () => ({ totals: zeroBuckets(), last: null }),
112	  apply: (state, event) => {
113	    let turn: number
114	    let step: number
115	    let usage: TokenUsage
116	    if (event.type === 'assistant/chunk' && event.data.chunk.type === 'usage') {
117	      ;({ turn, step } = event.data)
118	      usage = event.data.chunk.usage
119	    } else if (event.type === 'assistant/message' && event.data.usage !== undefined) {
120	      ;({ turn, step, usage } = event.data)
121	    } else {
122	      return state
123	    }
124	
125	    const buckets = bucketsFrom(usage)
126	    const previous = state.last !== null
127	      && state.last.turn === turn
128	      && state.last.step === step
129	      ? state.last.buckets
130	      : undefined
131	    if (previous !== undefined && bucketsEqual(previous, buckets)) return state
132	
133	    return {
134	      totals: addReplacing(state.totals, previous, buckets),
135	      last: { turn, step, buckets },
136	    }
137	  },
138	  view: state => state.totals,
139	  stateVersion: 1,
140	}
141	
142	/**
143	 * Token-meter's context-occupancy projection unit.
144	 *
145	 * Independent last-wins slots: the newest usage sample supplies the provider
146	 * numerator, the newest `request/context` record the denominator. Both are
147	 * whole values, so replay order alone decides the result and no cross-field
148	 * consistency is claimed — the pair is explicitly not one atomic request
149	 * observation (see {@link ContextPressureProjection}).
150	 *
151	 * `pressureTokens` is prompt-side only, so it holds still while a turn streams
152	 * and steps forward once the next request reports its usage. Because nothing
153	 * but a request reports usage, it also cannot see a compaction: the fold
154	 * therefore carries a running surface total alongside it and publishes
155	 * `projectedTokens` — the sample plus the surface's signed movement since it
156	 * was taken — so occupancy answers for the next request rather than the last
157	 * one. The total rides {@link foldSurfaceProjection}, so the state stays O(1)
158	 * and a replacement shrinks it by its logged shadow price. A replacement
159	 * without a claim preserves the previous total. A usage sample is stamped
160	 * BEFORE the same event joins the surface, so an `assistant/message` anchors
161	 * against the surface its own request saw.
162	 */
163	export const contextPressureProjectionDefinition:
164	ProjectionDefinition<'contextPressure', ContextPressureState> = {
165	  key: 'contextPressure',
166	  schema: pressureSchema,
167	  init: () => ({ surfaceTokens: 0 }),
168	  apply: (state, event) => {
169	    const fold = foldSurfaceProjection(state.claim, event)
170	    let next = state
171	    if (event.type === 'request/context') {
172	      const contextWindow = event.data.contextWindow
173	      if (contextWindow !== state.contextWindow) {
174	        if (contextWindow !== undefined) {
175	          next = { ...next, contextWindow }
176	        } else {
177	          const { contextWindow: _removed, ...withoutContextWindow } = next
178	          next = withoutContextWindow
179	        }
180	      }
181	    }
182	    const usage = usageOf(event)
183	    if (usage !== undefined) {
184	      const pressureTokens = pressureFrom(usage)
185	      if (pressureTokens !== next.pressureTokens || next.sampledSurfaceTokens !== next.surfaceTokens) {
186	        next = { ...next, pressureTokens, sampledSurfaceTokens: next.surfaceTokens }
187	      }
188	    }
189	    if (fold.deltaTokens !== 0) {
190	      next = { ...next, surfaceTokens: next.surfaceTokens + fold.deltaTokens }
191	    }
192	    // A defined fold.claim is always freshly built, so presence decides claim
193	    // bookkeeping: no claim before or after this event leaves `next` as is.
194	    if (state.claim === undefined && fold.claim === undefined) return next
195	    const { claim: _expired, ...withoutClaim } = next
196	    return fold.claim === undefined ? withoutClaim : { ...withoutClaim, claim: fold.claim }
197	  },
198	  view: ({ contextWindow, pressureTokens, surfaceTokens, sampledSurfaceTokens }) => ({
199	    ...contextWindow === undefined ? {} : { contextWindow },
200	    ...pressureTokens === undefined ? {} : { pressureTokens },
201	    ...pressureTokens === undefined || sampledSurfaceTokens === undefined
202	      ? {}
203	      : { projectedTokens: Math.max(0, pressureTokens + surfaceTokens - sampledSurfaceTokens) },
204	  }),
205	  stateVersion: 4,
206	}

1	/**
2	 * Pure session-log fold behind every budget decision. The policy plugin and the
3	 * invariant companion both read spend through it, so a recorded breach is
4	 * recomputable from the same events by anyone holding the log.
5	 *
6	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-budget-policy
7	 */
8	
9	import { assertNever } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
10	import type { SessionEvent } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
11	import type { BudgetCapId, BudgetRoutePricing, BudgetSpend } from './types.ts'
12	
13	/** Tokens per pricing unit; the table is quoted per one million tokens. */
14	const PRICING_UNIT_TOKENS = 1_000_000
15	
16	/** The pricing-table key one provider route is configured under. */
17	function routeKey(provider: string, model: string): string {
18	  return `${provider}/${model}`
19	}
20	
21	/**
22	 * Fold billed spend and elapsed wall time out of one session log.
23	 *
24	 * Only `assistant/message` carries a step's final provider accounting, so it is
25	 * the single usage source: the earlier `assistant/chunk` usage sample for the
26	 * same step is deliberately ignored rather than counted twice. Each message
27	 * prices against its own `provider/model` provenance, so a route switch mid
28	 * session bills each step at the rate configured for the route that served it;
29	 * a route absent from `pricing` contributes tokens but no cost.
30	 *
31	 * @param events - the session events to fold, oldest first.
32	 * @param pricing - EUR-per-million rates keyed by `provider/model`.
33	 * @returns the spend measured over exactly those events.
34	 */
35	export function foldBudgetSpend(
36	  events: readonly SessionEvent[],
37	  pricing: Readonly<Record<string, BudgetRoutePricing>>,
38	): BudgetSpend {
39	  let inputTokens = 0
40	  let outputTokens = 0
41	  let costEur = 0
42	  for (const event of events) {
43	    if (event.type !== 'assistant/message') continue
44	    const usage = event.data.usage
45	    if (usage === undefined) continue
46	    const input = usage.inputTokens + (usage.cacheReadTokens ?? 0) + (usage.cacheWriteTokens ?? 0)
47	    inputTokens += input
48	    outputTokens += usage.outputTokens
49	    const { provider, model } = event.data.message.source
50	    const rates = pricing[routeKey(provider, model)]
51	    if (rates === undefined) continue
52	    costEur += (input * rates.inputEurPerMillionTokens + usage.outputTokens * rates.outputEurPerMillionTokens)
53	      / PRICING_UNIT_TOKENS
54	  }
55	  const first = events[0]
56	  const last = events[events.length - 1]
57	  return {
58	    inputTokens,
59	    outputTokens,
60	    totalTokens: inputTokens + outputTokens,
61	    wallMs: first === undefined || last === undefined ? 0 : last.time - first.time,
62	    costEur,
63	  }
64	}
65	
66	/**
67	 * Read the spend one cap is measured against.
68	 * @param spend - folded session spend.
69	 * @param cap - the cap whose measurement is wanted.
70	 * @returns the measured value for that cap.
71	 */
72	export function measuredFor(spend: BudgetSpend, cap: BudgetCapId): number {
73	  switch (cap) {
74	    case 'maxInputTokens':
75	      return spend.inputTokens
76	    case 'maxOutputTokens':
77	      return spend.outputTokens
78	    case 'maxTotalTokens':
79	      return spend.totalTokens
80	    case 'maxWallMs':
81	      return spend.wallMs
82	    case 'maxCostEur':
83	      return spend.costEur
84	    /* v8 ignore next 2 -- BudgetCapId is closed and every member is handled above */
85	    default:
86	      return assertNever(cap, 'budget cap measurement')
87	  }
88	}

26	/**

29	 * first and last event times, so it counts idle gaps between events but not
